title: Bubble sort step by step
examples: Why is it called bubble sort?

stages.label: Start: 5 3 8 1
stages.note: Four towers in a muddled order

stages.label: Swap 5, 3: 3 5 8 1
stages.note: 5 is bigger than 3, so they swap

stages.label: Swap 8, 1: 3 5 1 8
stages.note: 5 and 8 are fine; 8 and 1 swap. 8 is home

stages.label: Swap 5, 1: 3 1 5 8
stages.note: Pass two: 1 bubbles left past 5

stages.label: Swap 3, 1: 1 3 5 8
stages.note: Pass three: one last swap

stages.label: Sorted!
stages.note: A pass with no swaps means we are done
stages.ask: How does bubble sort know it is finished?

explain.say: Imagine four friends lining up by height for a photo, all muddled up. How would a computer put them in order? Look at the board: four towers, 5, 3, 8 and 1. Our job is to sort them from smallest to biggest using bubble sort.
Here is the only rule: look at two neighbours. If the left one is bigger, swap them. Look at the second box: 5 and 3. 5 is bigger, so swap, and now we have 3, 5, 8, 1. What do we compare next?

explain.say: Next, 5 and 8 are already in order, so leave them. Then 8 and 1: swap! See the third box: 3, 5, 1, 8. The biggest number has bubbled all the way to the end, like a bubble rising in water. Is the list sorted yet?

explain.say: Not yet, so we do another pass, which means going along the line again. 5 and 1 swap, then on pass three, 3 and 1 swap. Look at the board: 1, 3, 5, 8! How do we know we can stop?

explain.say: Yes, one last pass with no swaps tells us it is finished. Look how neat the towers are now! Brilliant sorting. Wow fact: bubble sort is simple but slow; for a million items, faster methods like merge sort win by miles. Challenge: bubble sort the numbers 4, 2, 3, 1 yourself.

faq.a: Bubble sort walks along the list comparing each pair of neighbours and swaps them if they are in the wrong order. It repeats these passes until a pass makes no swaps.

faq.q: How does bubble sort know it is finished?
faq.a: When it makes a full pass along the list without swapping anything, every pair is in order, so the whole list is sorted.
asks: How many passes does bubble sort need?

faq.q: Why is it called bubble sort?
faq.a: Because on each pass the biggest unsorted item moves to the end, like a bubble rising to the top of water.
asks: Where does the name bubble sort come from?

faq.a: A sorting algorithm is a set of steps for putting items in order, like smallest to biggest or A to Z. Bubble sort, insertion sort and merge sort are examples.
Not for big lists. Doubling the list size roughly makes it four times slower. Merge sort and quicksort are much faster for large amounts of data, but bubble sort is easy to understand.
asks: What is faster than bubble sort?

facts: In bubble sort, after each pass the largest unsorted item is in its final place at the end.
For a list of n items, bubble sort may need about n × n comparisons in the worst case.

quiz.say: In bubble sort, what do you do if the left neighbour is bigger than the right one?
quiz.show: Left is bigger than right. You…
quiz.why: Bubble sort swaps neighbours that are in the wrong order.

wrong.1: Leaving them keeps the wrong order.
wrong.2: Sorting never throws data away; it only reorders it.

quiz.say: After the first pass of bubble sort, where is the biggest number?
quiz.show: After pass one, the biggest number is…

options.show: At the end of the list
options.say: At the end of the list

quiz.why: The biggest number keeps winning each comparison, so it bubbles all the way to the end.

wrong.1: The start is where the smallest number will finish.
wrong.2: It keeps moving right until it reaches the end.
